topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Slope vs. Area
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the slope of a curve.
Integrals calculate the area under a curve.
These two concepts seem completely unrelated.
animations: Create a coordinate system, plot a straight line y=f(x). (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight a segment under the curve as area. (Color: #FF00FF)
Show the slope of the tangent at point x. (Color: #00FFFF)

sections.title: The Conceptual Link: Inverse Operations
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse processes.
They behave like addition and subtraction.
One operation reverses the other completely.
animations: Represent differentiation as breaking down a function. (Color: #FFCC00)
Represent integration as building up a function. (Color: #00FFCC)
Show the two operations canceling each other out. (Color: #FFFFFF)

sections.title: The Accumulation Function
lecture_lines: Define an accumulation function for area.
animations: Draw the accumulation function A(x) = integral from a to x. (Color: #FF00FF)
As x increases, show the area A(x) growing. (Color: #00FFFF)
Label the relationship between f(t) and A(x). (Color: #FFFF00)
Highlight the rate of change of A(x). (Color: #FF0000)
